summary:
All six fixes are in the tree, and they do what the findings asked.

**What I ran:**
- Built and ran the full default suite: 394 passed.
- Ran the SL-063 bug catalog: 10 passed.
- Ran a mutation check. I put back `!_fullClass` at Scanner.cs:469 and removed the `free > total` guard in Kernel32.TryUsedBytes. Exactly the five new case tests failed, all three HF-001 Theory rows and the Fact showing `Actual: True`. Then I restored the tree with `git checkout`.

So both case tests feed their shape through the code:
- **C-001:** a real NTFS hardlinked pair, listed under the extended class, with each of the three "no ID" values fed in through the ListedFileId seam.
- **C-002:** a 100 GiB quota total against 626 GiB of volume free space.

**Blocker:** a declared architecture rule is broken. The HF-003 change added `using FsAnalyser.Core.Store;` to src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs:2. That matches the .taad/fitness.yaml rule "the window never touches the scan store" (`(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b`, every App file except FolderTree*.cs). Fitness op=check now reports this line as VIOLATED, and it is the only violation in the tree.

The xUnit ArchitectureRulesTests has no copy of this rule, which is why the suite stayed green. The builder's account says it read the fitness patterns for the edited files and that all still hold. For this rule that is not true.

HF-003's premise was partly wrong: "the App already uses EntryKind" is only true in the FolderTree files, which the rule exempts. The build did not declare that it crossed the rule.

**Other checks, all clean:**
- The removed symbols (TopLevelKind, ScanProgress.Links, VolumeSpace.DefaultBound, the IO_REPARSE_TAG_* constants) have no remaining references. I also checked the window hook, StallRig and the bug tests, which are outside FsAnalyser.slnx and would not fail the build.
- The --report schema does not serialize TopLevelRow.Kind, so the enum's numbers changing (Folder=0 against File=0) reaches no report consumer.
- VolumeSpace behaves the same as before for drive roots, now via LongPath.ToDisplay.
- The builder's declared departures hold as described: the ListedFileId test seam; the "no file lacked an ID" rule, under which a full-class scan with no files now reports true; and taking ToDisplay rather than dropping the prefix handling.

Second round: This second round found one new defect, a minor one. B1 from the first round still stands, so the verdict stays needs-fixes.

**The new defect (m1):** `Kernel32.TryUsedBytes` still wraps to a negative number for one input. It guards against free being larger than total. But if total less free is larger than `long.MaxValue`, the `(long)` cast still gives a negative "used" figure. The project does not turn on overflow checking, so the cast wraps silently. That is the same failure HF-024 was meant to close, reached by a different input. It would take a volume that says it holds more than 8 EiB, which is unlikely but not ruled out by the API.

**Checked and clean:**
- **What counts as "no ID":** the scanner's count (Scanner.cs:327) and the store's deduplication (ScanStore.cs:244-248) apply the same test to the same entries. `ScanStore.Append` deduplicates every file that has an ID, whatever its other flags, and a cloud-only file is still a file. `AddEntry` is the only place listed entries are added.
- **Cancelled listings:** a listing that Cancel aborts never reaches `AddEntry`, so the new count cannot include files that were then discarded.
- **Switching listing class mid-scan:** when the scanner falls back to the older class, the files it lists afterwards carry ID 0. They are counted, so the result is the same as the old class-based rule.
- **Nothing reads IDs later:** the probe pass reads no file IDs, so nothing can deduplicate a file after it was counted as having no ID.
- **The window:** the file-ID note goes into `OutcomeNotes`, not `OutcomeDetail`. So the line-count checks in WindowCases.ps1 (V-001) are not affected when a share now shows the note.
- **`LongPath.ToDisplay` inputs:** a UNC path, a device path or a volume GUID path all give the same `IsDriveRoot` answer as before.
- **The default time limit:** `Task.Delay(bound)` behaves as it did before with the default of 30 s. The only other caller that reads the error code from `TryGetVolumeUsed` is a test of a drive letter with no volume behind it.
- **Input formats:** the diff adds no parser, regular expression or reader, so there were no format inputs to try.

findings.claim:
The HF-003 change breaks the project's declared architecture rule "the window never touches the scan store". TopLevelRowText.cs now imports the FsAnalyser.Core.Store namespace so it can compare `row.Kind != EntryKind.Folder`, and the rule forbids naming `.Store` in any App file outside FolderTree*.cs.

Fitness op=check reports the rule as VIOLATED at exactly this line; the tree had no violation before this diff. The xUnit suite does not carry this rule (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:141-155 only checks `\bScanStore\b`), so the 394 green tests say nothing about it.

The build did not declare the crossing, and its own account claims the fitness patterns for the edited files all still hold. HF-003's premise that "the App already uses EntryKind" is only true in FolderTree*.cs, which the rule exempts by name. The slice will fail the fitness gate as written.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs:2 `using FsAnalyser.Core.Store;` and :38 `if (row.Kind != EntryKind.Folder)`. .taad/fitness.yaml:396-418: the rule "the window never touches the scan store", files src/FsAnalyser.App/**/*.cs, must_not_match '(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b', except_files src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTree*.cs. mcp Fitness op=check: 'VIOLATED ... src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs:2 matches /(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b/'.
findings.fix:
Stop TopLevelRowText from naming the Store namespace. The smallest change:
1. Add `public bool IsFolder => Kind == EntryKind.Folder;` to TopLevelRow in src/FsAnalyser.Core/TopLevelSnapshot.cs.
2. In TopLevelRowText.FiguresOf, test `!row.IsFolder`.
3. Delete the `using FsAnalyser.Core.Store;` line.

If narrowing the rule is preferred instead (an enum reads nothing from the store), make it a declared change to .taad/fitness.yaml with its reason. Do not add TopLevelRowText.cs to except_files, which would also let `.Store` reads through.

findings.claim:
TryUsedBytes still returns true with a negative used figure for one input the API allows. GetDiskFreeSpaceExW returns two unsigned 64-bit values. When total less free is larger than long.MaxValue, `(long)(total - free)` wraps negative, because the project does not turn on overflow checking. For example, a total of ulong.MaxValue with 0 free gives -1.

The guard only covers free > total, so VolumeSpace.Read reports the figure as valid. MainWindow.Coverage then prints 'The volume reports <negative> in use; this scan counted ... more than that'. That is the exact symptom HF-024 describes, reached through the other bound.

The new test's own docstring promises 'no figure, never the negative one the subtraction wraps to', and the function breaks that for this input. Only a volume, most likely a remote or virtual one, that claims a total above 8 EiB could trigger it. None is known on this machine.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/Kernel32.cs:174-183: `if (free > total) { used = 0; return false; } used = (long)(total - free); return true;`. No CheckForOverflowUnderflow in any src csproj or Directory.Build.props (grep: no matches). VolumeSpace.cs:58 passes any true result through as the figure. MainWindow.xaml.cs:682-686 (Coverage) prints volumeInUse as it is. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/VolumeUsageTests.cs:95-104 tests only free > total and an ordinary difference.
findings.fix: In TryUsedBytes, change the guard to `if (free > total || total - free > long.MaxValue)`. Add a matching assert to AFreeFigureAboveTheQuotaTotalIsNoFigure: `Assert.False(Kernel32.TryUsedBytes(ulong.MaxValue, 0, out _))`.

obligations.evidence:
The fix: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs:315 applies the ListedFileId seam, :327-328 counts `_filesWithoutId` for each file that fails ScanStore.HasFileId, and :469 sets `FileIdsAvailable = status != RootUnreadable && _filesWithoutId == 0`.

The tests: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ListingFallbackTests.cs TheExtendedClassListingNoFileIdsSaysSo (a Theory over 0, all ones, and the widened 64-bit all ones) scans a real NTFS hardlinked pair under the default extended class. It asserts 2000 bytes (both names charged) and FileIdsAvailable false. OneFileListedWithoutAnIdIsEnoughToSaySo covers the case where only some files lack an ID.

Checked by running: I put `!_fullClass` back, the four tests failed with Actual: True, and I restored the file.

The fix: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/Kernel32.cs:160 `return TryUsedBytes(total, free, out used);`, and :174-183 returns false when free > total. VolumeSpace.Read (VolumeSpace.cs:58) turns false into a null figure.

The test: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/VolumeUsageTests.cs AFreeFigureAboveTheQuotaTotalIsNoFigure feeds a 100 GiB total with 626 GiB free and expects false. It also checks that the reversed figures still subtract.

Checked by running: without the guard the test fails, and with it the test passes. No real per-user quota was set; that needs an administrator, and no named elevated operation covers it.

cases.evidence:
tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ListingFallbackTests.cs builds a real NTFS TempTree with x.txt hardlinked as y.txt and scans it under the extended class (ForceFullDirectoryClass is not set). Through ScanOptions.ListedFileId it replaces every listed ID with 0, UInt128.MaxValue, or new UInt128(0, ulong.MaxValue), the three values HasFileId rules out.

It asserts both names are charged (2000 bytes) and FileIdsAvailable is false. A companion Fact zeroes only z.txt's ID and asserts 1050 bytes and false.

The mutation run confirmed all four fail against the old `!_fullClass` rule.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/VolumeUsageTests.cs AFreeFigureAboveTheQuotaTotalIsNoFigure calls Kernel32.TryUsedBytes(100 GiB, 626 GiB): the quota shape, with free above total. It expects false.

TryGetVolumeUsed's only success path now returns through this function (Kernel32.cs:160). The mutation run confirmed the test fails without the guard. A real quota was not set up (it needs an administrator); the shape is fed in as the raw pair of figures.

drift: HF-003 is built as designed (TopLevelRow.Kind is now an EntryKind), but getting there made src/FsAnalyser.App/TopLevelRowText.cs import FsAnalyser.Core.Store. That crosses the fitness rule "the window never touches the scan store", and the build did not declare it. The build account also says the fitness patterns for the edited files 'all still hold', which is wrong for this rule. Filed as B1.

HF-001 (declared): FileIdsAvailable now means 'no listed file lacked an ID'. A full-class scan that lists no files, or a scan cancelled before any file was listed, now reports true where it used to report false. No test pins that shape; the builder declared it.

HF-001 (declared follow-up): MainWindow.xaml.cs:491 still says 'This drive does not report file IDs'. That is now also shown when only some files lacked an ID, so the wording over-states the cause in that case.

No new drift this round. The first round's items stand: B1, the undeclared crossing of the fitness rule in TopLevelRowText.cs:2, and the declared change to what FileIdsAvailable means when no files were listed.
